paper_metadata.title: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models
paper_metadata.abstract: Recent advances demonstrate that scaling Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) effectively improves downstream task performances. However, existing scaling methods enable all model parameters to be active for each token in the calculation, which brings massive training and inferring costs. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective training strategy MoE-Tuning for LVLMs. This strategy innovatively addresses the common issue of performance degradation in multi-modal sparsity learning, consequently constructing a sparse model with an outrageous number of parameters but a constant computational cost. Furthermore, we present the MoE-LLaVA, a MoE-based sparse LVLM architecture, which uniquely activates only the top-k experts through routers during deployment, keeping the remaining experts inactive. Extensive experiments show the significant performance of MoE-LLaVA in a variety of visual understanding and object hallucination benchmarks. Remarkably, with only approximately 3B sparsely activated parameters, MoE-LLaVA demonstrates performance comparable to the LLaVA-1.5-7B on various visual understanding datasets and even surpasses the LLaVA-1.5-13B in object hallucination benchmark. Through MoE-LLaVA, we aim to establish a baseline for sparse LVLMs and provide valuable insights for future research in developing more efficient and effective multi-modal learning systems. Code is released at https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/MoE-LLaVA.

extraction_data.innovation: MoE-Tuning: a novel three-stage training strategy for adapting Mixture-of-Experts to LVLMs that prevents performance degradation caused by sparsity; uniquely activates only top-k experts through routers during deployment, keeping computational cost constant while scaling model capacity; differs from prior dense scaling methods by maintaining fixed computational cost per token despite massive parameter growth, directly addressing the performance degradation common in multi-modal sparsity learning.
extraction_data.application: Visual understanding, object hallucination mitigation, multi-modal learning
extraction_data.research_problem: Scaling Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) efficiently by reducing training and inference costs while maintaining or improving performance through sparse activation.
extraction_data.paper_title: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models
extraction_data.training_pipeline: 3-stage MoE-Tuning: Stage I trains only MLP; Stage II trains all parameters except Vision Encoder; Stage III uses FFNs to initialize experts and trains only MoE layers
extraction_data.moe_configuration: 4 experts, top-2 activated per token via router
extraction_data.benchmark_result: POPE (Adversarial/Random/Popular average); ScienceQA; MMBench; LLaVAW; MM-Vet (outperforms LLaVA-1.5-7B by 1.9%, 0.4%, 0.9%, 30.7%, and 3.8% respectively)

extraction_data.innovation: Soft-router Mixture of Experts (MoE) for LVLMs: uses a lightweight linear router to predict token-to-expert assignment probabilities, enabling dynamic data allocation among experts for sparsity and reduced interference; three-stage training (visual projection adaptation, dense LVLM tuning, MoE tuning) to stabilize sparse model learning.

extraction_data.research_problem: Reducing the cost of scaling up dense visual data and models for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by leveraging model sparsity.
extraction_data.application: Image understanding, multi-modal instruction following, image logical reasoning, text recognition

extraction_data.innovation: Replaces dense feed-forward networks (FFNs) with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers in large vision-language models; uses a router to compute token-to-expert matching weights, activates top-k experts per token, and aggregates outputs via weighted summation; incorporates a differentiable load balancing loss to ensure balanced expert utilization, enabling infinitely sparse pathways and improved parameter efficiency.
